gtk.title: Pushchairs and buggies
gtk.text: The whole site is grass, which can be bumpy and soft after rain. I have found a pushchair with big wheels copes much better than a small buggy.

gtk.title: Dogs
gtk.text: Dogs are welcome on a lead. I would bring water for them, and think about a quiet spot away from the crowd line if your dog is nervous of loud engines.

gtk.title: Your own food and drink
gtk.text: A picnic is a great way to save money, and I would bring plenty of water. When I last checked nothing said if you can bring your own alcohol, so I would ask the show before you pack any.

gtk.title: Gazebos, windbreaks and chairs
gtk.text: I would bring chairs, as there’s no seating on the grass. Nothing I could find says if gazebos or windbreaks are allowed, so I would ask the organisers first and keep anything tall to the back.

gtk.title: Water refill points
gtk.text: I couldn’t find anything about refill points. There’s very little shade, so I would bring more water than you think you need.

gtk.title: Changing Places toilet
gtk.text: At a recent show there were portable toilets, including an accessible one, just inside the gate. A Changing Places toilet isn’t mentioned, so I would ask the show before you go if you need one.

gtk.title: Carers’ tickets
gtk.text: I couldn’t find a carer ticket listed. It’s a volunteer run charity show, so I would message the organisers through the contact page and ask.

gtk.title: Hearing support
gtk.text: Nothing says if there’s a hearing loop or BSL. I would ask the show before you go, and agree a meeting point with your group in case you can’t hear the commentary.

gtk.title: Quiet area
gtk.text: There’s no quiet or sensory space listed. The west end of the crowd line is usually the calmer side, away from the busiest stalls, so this may work for you.

gtk.title: Re-entry
gtk.text: You can leave and come back. I would keep your wristband on, as you need it to get back in.

gtk.title: First aid and lost children
gtk.text: I couldn’t find where the first aid point is, so I would ask a steward when you arrive. Agree a meeting point by the car show and write your phone number on younger children’s wrists.

gtk.title: If it rains
gtk.text: Unfortunately the weather on the day will be what it will be, so plan accordingly. If it’s fresh, dress in layers to keep warm. Displays may be changed for safety, but the show carries on.

ground.html:
The Ground Show

The flying doesn’t start until around lunchtime, so the morning is yours to walk round. It’s a compact grass site, and I think that’s the beauty of it. You can see the aircraft, the cars, the stalls and the food in a couple of hours without rushing, and still be back on your chair before the first display.

CostIncluded in your ticket
Gates10:00 (2026)
Car show300+ vehicles
Craft fairInside the hangars (2026)

Things To See

Free

Aircraft On The Grass

Vintage biplanes and visiting aircraft park on the grass near the crowd line. Some owners open their aircraft up so you can take a look inside, and you may find exclusive merch for sale in or beside them. I would go in the morning, before the crowds and while the light is soft.

Free

Watch Them Taxi Out

Little Gransden is a working airfield and home to the Global Stars aerobatic team. Aircraft taxi out close to the crowd at the quieter west end, and children love to see that.

Free

The Car Lines

More than 300 classic, vintage and specialist cars and motorbikes, and the owners are usually happy to chat. Fancy putting yours in? Take a look at .

Free to browse

Craft Fair In The Hangars

In 2026 the craft and artisan stalls were set up inside the aircraft hangars. That’s handy if a shower comes over, and I would leave a little room in the bag for a gift.

Free to browse

Trade Stalls

The trade stalls are outdoors, with some right along the flightline. Clothes, pet treats, prints and gifts all turn up. Some may only take cash, so I would bring a little as well as a card.

Pay as you go

The Food Village

In 2026 there were fifteen food village pitches, so there’s a fair choice. I would eat before 12:30 to beat the queue. More in .

Free

Live Music

There’s live music through the day, which fills the gaps between the displays nicely if your group isn’t all into aircraft.

Rides extra

The Funfair

There was a funfair at the 2024 show. I haven’t seen it confirmed for 2027 yet, so I wouldn’t promise the children rides until it is.

How I Would Do The Morning

  1. Save your pitch firstIf you want a front row seat, head to the crowd line when the gates open and put your chairs down. The centre fills first.
  2. Then walk roundTake a look at the aircraft on the grass, speak to the pilots if they’re about, walk the car lines and visit the stalls. Check the food options while you’re there.
  3. Toilets before the flyingI would go before the first display at around 12:30. If there’s a display you aren’t waiting to see, use it as a toilet break.
  4. Stay on at the endIn 2026 the traders were asked to stay open until at least 18:00. Have another look round after the flying and let the lanes clear before you leave.
Jack’s tipThe whole day raises money for BBC Children in Need and local children’s charities. I would keep some coins in your pocket for the collections. Children love to hear their day out is helping other children.

Based on the 2026 show. Stalls, food and entertainment change each year, so please check nearer the day.

skipped.days: One day show (Sunday 29 August 2027), so there is no day to pick.
skipped.flights: I could not find any pleasure, helicopter or warbird flights offered at or from Little Gransden for visitors, so I left it out rather than list a company I can't confirm.
skipped.support: It is a ticketed show, not a free one. The charity fundraising (BBC Children in Need) is mentioned in the ground section tip instead.

notes: The official site (https://littlegransdenairshow.co.uk/) is now just a holding page: home, contact and privacy only. The old visitor information, air display, car exhibitor and trade stall pages have gone, so I couldn't recheck the dogs, re-entry, ear defender, accessibility and weather details today. I reused what the page already says for those tiles and marked the rest as not confirmed. The page's links already point to the home page, which is fine, but the labels such as 'Official visitor information', 'Air display' and 'Car exhibitor information' now open a page that doesn't have that information. The ticket link (https://ticketflex.io/tickets/little-gransden-air-and-car-show) still shows the 2026 show on 30 August 2026, so 2027 tickets aren't on sale yet. The home page says the 2026 total raised for Children in Need will be announced in November on Facebook (https://www.facebook.com/littlegransden), so the 'more than £400,000' figure may need updating soon. The 2026 trader form (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfj6bG1bo2cOK1YHSzIOG-O3VJwvN9y0deio6m0VvLJVKoy9Q/viewform) puts craft and artisan stalls inside the hangars, lists 15 food village pitches and a trader closing date of 31 July, and asks traders to stay open until at least 18:00. The 'Show Your Car Or Stall' section says no closing date was listed, which is now out of date for trade stalls. The funfair is only confirmed for 2024 (Hunts Post, https://huntspost.co.uk/news/24529528.little-gransden-air-car-show-airfield-august-25). That article also gave 2024 flying as 13:00 to 17:00, while the page uses about 12:30 for 2026.
